objective.Feedback_O: The forecast was good and the cyclone exceeded the threshold. You acted in time and reached the affected communities.
The threshold was exceeded, but supplies were not distributed before landfall.
The warning justified action. You missed an opportunity to help.
You acted in time but left some affected areas uncovered.
The intervention reached people, but distributing everywhere was unnecessarily expensive.
The warning came too late for the required action. This was not a preventable failure by the player.
The storm made landfall above the threshold, but the forecast did not justify action. Your restraint was defensible on the basis of the forecast available to you.
The storm made landfall above the threshold, but the available forecast did not justify the action. A good outcome is not necessarily a good decision.
Action was initiated too late to complete distribution before impact.
Assistance was delivered away from the areas actually affected.
The threshold was not exceeded and the forecast did not justify activation. Conserving funds was appropriate.
The forecast did not justify action and the threshold was not exceeded.
The threshold was not exceeded, but prepositioning was justified by the available warning.
The forecast justified activation, even though the storm ultimately stayed below threshold.
The outcome was benign, but the warning suggested action. You may have been lucky.
The threshold was exceeded, but earlier spending left no money for this response.
Rapid intensification left too little time to complete the required intervention.
The forecast displaced the impact area, so even reasonable targeting missed affected communities.
You acted decisively under uncertainty and reached affected areas.
Your response was well targeted but budget constraints limited coverage.
You reached affected communities, but also mobilised supplies in locations that were not directly affected. Those funds may have been better reserved for later storms.

You reached affected communities, but also fully activated in locations that were not directly affected. Distribution in those locations increased expenditure without adding to the game's modelled reach.
You reached some affected communities but left others unsupported, while committing funds to locations that were not directly affected. This reduced the efficiency of your response.
You mobilised when the available forecast supported doing so.
You mobilised even though the forecast available on the decision day did not meet the mobilisation trigger.
The mobilisation trigger was reached while action was still possible, but you did not mobilise.
The mobilisation trigger was not reached while action was possible, and you appropriately conserved the budget.
Some mobilisation decisions were supported by the forecast at the time, but others were not.
There was no eligible mobilisation decision window in the recorded briefings, so this stage cannot be assessed.
You fully activated when the available forecast supported doing so.
You fully activated even though the forecast available on the decision day did not meet the full-activation trigger.
The full-activation trigger was reached while action was possible, but no full activation was completed.
The full-activation trigger was not reached during the eligible window, so restraint was consistent with the forecast.
Some full-activation decisions were supported by the forecast at the time, but others were not.
There was no eligible full-activation decision window in the recorded briefings, so this stage cannot be assessed.
The full-activation trigger was reached, but no warehouse had been mobilised in advance, so activation was not possible.

boss.Feedback_B: We helped {people_reached} people before the storm. The donor is delighted!
We helped {people_reached} people! But I am worried about what we have left for the next storm.
Well, that gamble paid off! I hope you are not planning to rely on luck all season.
Excellent work, but have we spent too much of the season's budget?
People were affected and we did nothing. The donor is furious, whatever the forecast said.
We could not have anticipated this, but it is still very difficult to explain.
We had a warning and we failed to act. I need an explanation.
No impact in the end, and we saved money. Perhaps you knew something I didn't!
Good restraint. We can keep our resources for the next storm.
I understand why you acted, but the donor is asking why we spent money on a near miss.
That false alarm has cost us dearly. How are we going to manage the rest of the season?
We reached {people_reached} people. Good work, although some communities were missed.
At least some people received help, but the spending and targeting are hard to defend.
We followed the warning, but the cyclone struck somewhere else. The donor will want answers.
How could the storm intensify so quickly? We need a better system.
A great result for this storm. But what happens if another one comes?
We have spent the budget and still failed to reach people. This is serious.
The donor is pleased with the result. I am less convinced by how we got there.
You made a sensible call, but I am still worried about the money we have left.
You did what you could with the warning we had. Unfortunately the outcome looks poor.
